title: Add KMS preflight validation, permission checks, and audit-friendly validation report
author: Bruno Silva
description: Context: We keep seeing Private installs fail late (or worse: succeed but later decrypt fails) due to KMS misconfiguration: wrong key ARN/region, missing IAM actions, key disabled, policy doesn’t allow the installer principal, or customer KMS throttling. This PR adds an explicit KMS preflight step to the Private installer so we fail fast with actionable output, and we produce an audit-friendly validation report that customers can attach to change tickets/security evidence. Summary of changes (high level): 1) New installer preflight stage: "kms" runs by default when KMS envelope encryption is configured (and can also be invoked explicitly via `redwood-private-installer validate kms`). 2) Permission + configuration checks with actionable remediation: resolves KMS key identifier, validates region alignment, validates key state (enabled, not pending deletion), and performs a safe Encrypt/Decrypt round-trip using a short-lived random payload (never persisted). The checks are mapped into a small set of installer error codes and messages that line up with the platform-wide KMS error taxonomy (AccessDenied, NotFound, Throttling, Timeout, InvalidCiphertext, DisabledKey). 3) Audit/ops report generation: on every run (success or failure), write a structured JSON report to `./reports/kms-preflight-<timestamp>.json` (override via `--report-path`). Report includes: installer version/build, timestamp, deployment id/cluster name (if available), cloud provider, key identifier (redacted by default), principal ARN/subject (redacted by default), each check result, latency per call, AWS request IDs (or equivalent), and a top-level pass/fail summary. Sensitive fields are excluded (no plaintext, no ciphertext, no auth headers, no full policy documents). 4) Guardrails: `--skip-kms-preflight` remains available for break-glass/airgapped bootstrap flows, but now requires `--i-understand-kms-risk` and emits a prominent warning in stdout and the report. 5) Support ergonomics: error output now includes “what we tried”, “what failed”, and “how to fix” sections with copy/paste IAM action lists, plus a hint to attach the report file when opening a support ticket. Implementation notes: - AWS KMS: uses DescribeKey + Encrypt/Decrypt round-trip. We intentionally do NOT call GenerateDataKey to avoid requiring broader permissions than runtime decrypt/encrypt needs in some deployments; the installer validates the minimum runtime envelope path. - Timeouts/retries: preflight uses conservative timeouts (2s per call, max 2 retries w/ jitter) to avoid long hangs during install. Throttling is reported clearly with suggested next steps (quota/limit, backoff, or allowlist of installer IP if applicable). - Redaction: by default key ARN is truncated to last 12 chars, principal is truncated to account + role name; `--report-include-identifiers` will include full identifiers if the operator chooses (still excludes secrets). - Output format stability: report JSON includes a `schema_version` field for future parsing by audit pipelines. Testing: - Unit tests for redaction, error mapping, and report serialization. - A small mocked KMS client harness that simulates AccessDenied/NotFound/Throttling/Timeout/DisabledKey and asserts installer output and report contents. - CI adds a smoke run for `validate kms` on a stubbed config (no real cloud creds) to ensure the stage wiring doesn’t regress. Operator-facing behavior (examples): - Missing permission -> installer fails with: "KMS preflight failed: AccessDenied on Decrypt. Ensure the installer principal has kms:Decrypt on <key>. See report: reports/kms-preflight-...json" and includes a minimal IAM snippet. - Wrong region -> installer fails with: "KMS key region mismatch: key is in us-west-2 but deployment configured for us-east-1". - Throttling -> installer fails with: "KMS throttling detected (429/ThrottlingException). Reduce parallelism, check KMS quotas, or retry later. See report for request IDs and latencies." Checklist: [x] Backwards compatible (new preflight only runs when KMS is enabled; skip flag available) [x] Report contains no secrets and is safe to attach to change tickets [x] Error messages include remediation hints [x] Added tests for key failure modes. Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Hook report export into the broader "evidence pack" generation flow (see ENG-4826). - Add GCP/Azure native KMS provider implementations in installer (today we validate AWS KMS path; other providers remain config-validated only).
commits: installer: add KMS preflight stage wiring + CLI entrypoint
kms: implement AWS KMS validator (DescribeKey + Encrypt/Decrypt round-trip)
installer: add structured report writer with schema_version + redaction helpers
installer: map KMS failures to canonical taxonomy + actionable messages
tests: add mocked KMS harness for AccessDenied/NotFound/Throttle/Timeout/DisabledKey
docs: update installer output hints for attaching KMS preflight report to support tickets
ci_checks: installer smoke (validate kms w/ mocked client): pass
review_conversation: Hanae Suzuki (Security): Please confirm the report cannot leak plaintext/ciphertext or full key policies. Also prefer redaction-on by default. Author: Confirmed; report excludes plaintext/ciphertext entirely and does not fetch policy documents. Default is redaction-on, with an explicit `--report-include-identifiers` override.

Jordan Lee (Policy): The remediation hint should list the minimum IAM actions required. Also clarify that installer and runtime roles can be different. Author: Added per-check IAM action lists (DescribeKey, Encrypt, Decrypt) and a note in output/report that installer principal may differ from runtime principal; the preflight validates the principal actually executing the installer.

Sean Gallagher (SRE): Watch out for long installs if KMS is degraded; keep retry budgets tight and include request IDs for provider escalation. Author: Set 2s per-call timeout, 2 retries w/ jitter, and included request IDs + per-call latency in the report. Also added explicit Throttling messaging.

Vivek Kulkarni (Private Deployments): We need a break-glass path for airgapped bootstrap but it must be loud. Author: Kept `--skip-kms-preflight` but required `--i-understand-kms-risk` and wrote the skip decision into the report.

Kira Thompson (Docs): Can we point operators to attach the report to support tickets? Author: Added a standard footer line to failure output and to the report header: “Attach this file to Redwood Support for faster triage.”
